items.title: Boundary gate timing and default
items.statement: The LSP diagnostics gate is evaluated before promotion at enabled phase, task, or subtask boundaries; it is opt-in, defaults to the phase boundary, and advisory iteration preflight cannot replace the configured boundary gate.

evidence.exact_quote: - **When it runs:** At configured **tier boundaries** before promotion. It MAY be enabled for `phase`, `task`, and/or `subtask`; default: **phase boundary only**. Implementations MAY also run an iteration-local preflight, but that is advisory and MUST NOT replace the configured boundary gate.
- `enabled`: **false** (opt-in per project)

items.title: Gate scopes and changed-file default
items.statement: The gate accepts changed_files, open, or project scope and defaults to changed_files; each scope requires a concrete path set from execution, editor, or project/LSP state.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Scope:** What files are checked. One of:
- **`project`** -- All project files that have an LSP server (bounded: e.g. under project root, or only files with open documents). Default: **`changed_files`** to keep checks fast and relevant.

items.title: Severity pass criteria
items.statement: The diagnostic threshold has two semantic modes: errors only, or errors and warnings; Info never blocks and the default semantics are errors only.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`error`** -- Gate passes if there are **no diagnostics with severity Error** in scope. Warnings and Info are ignored.
- **`error_and_warning`** -- Gate passes if there are **no diagnostics with severity Error or Warning** in scope. Info is ignored.

items.title: Verification settings surface
items.statement: The Verification tab exposes enable, scope, blocking threshold, tier-boundary, and timeout controls, persisted with VerificationConfig.

evidence.exact_quote: - **GUI:** Verification tab: "LSP diagnostics gate" subsection: Enable checkbox; Scope dropdown (Changed files / Open files / Whole project); Block on (Errors only / Errors and warnings); Tier boundaries (checkboxes: Phase, Task, Subtask); Timeout (seconds). Persist in same config blob as `VerificationConfig` (e.g. extend `VerificationConfig` or nested `lsp_gate`).

items.title: Gate failure propagation
items.statement: A blocking diagnostic produces an unmet LSP criterion and failed tier gate; the orchestrator then follows the ordinary retry, escalate, or stop transition configured for that tier.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Gate fails (LSP errors in scope):** The gate report for that tier has `passed: false`; the **criterion** for the LSP gate has `met: false` and `actual` set to a summary (e.g. "3 LSP errors in scope (see evidence)").

- **Orchestrator behavior:** Same as for any failed gate: **retry** (next iteration) if retry policy allows; else **escalate** or **stop** per tier config (e.g. `task_failure_style`). No special case for LSP gate.

items.title: User-visible failure reporting
items.statement: Dashboard and Gate report consume the failed criterion, an optional toast can summarize the error count, and attached LSP evidence supports inspection.

evidence.exact_quote: - **User notification:** Standard gate failure path: Dashboard/Gate report shows failure; optional toast "LSP gate failed: N errors in scope." Evidence (LSP snapshot) is attached so user can inspect.

items.title: Snapshot captured on every gate run
items.statement: Each actual gate evaluation captures and links an LSP diagnostics snapshot regardless of pass or fail.

evidence.exact_quote: - **When:** When the LSP gate **runs** (whether it passes or fails), attach an **LSP diagnostics snapshot** to the gate report. So: **always** capture snapshot at gate run time; store it as evidence linked to that gate run.

items.title: Verifier and registry execution authority
items.statement: LspGateVerifier owns diagnostic evaluation and snapshot evidence production, while VerifierRegistry resolves the criterion and the unchanged gate runner aggregates the result.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Who calls LSP:** A new verifier **`LspGateVerifier`** (or **`lsp_gate_verifier`**), registered in `VerifierRegistry` (e.g. in `verifier.rs` `register_defaults`). Criterion type: `verification_method: "lsp"` or `"lsp_gate"`.

- **Gate runner:** No change to gate_runner flow: it already dispatches by `criterion.verification_method` to the registry; when the criterion is LSP gate, the registry returns `LspGateVerifier`, which runs.

items.title: Diagnostic query input and output
items.statement: The LSP client accepts paths and a project root and returns diagnostic entries containing location, severity, message, and source; paths without a server or diagnostics contribute no entries.

evidence.exact_quote: - Signature (conceptual): `get_diagnostics_for_paths(paths: &[PathBuf], project_root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<LspDiagnosticEntry>, LspGateError>`.

- Returns: list of diagnostics (path, line, character, severity, message, source) for the given paths. If a path has no server or no diagnostics, it contributes an empty list. The client uses the existing DiagnosticsCache (from `publishDiagnostics`) and/or triggers a request if needed; must respect timeout (e.g. 15 s) and return partial results or error on timeout.

items.title: Snapshot representation and coordinate normalization
items.statement: Snapshot entries preserve path, one-based line, zero-based character, severity, message, optional source, and optional code, converting line coordinates only at the LSP protocol boundary.

evidence.exact_quote: - **line** -- 0-based or 1-based per LSP spec (LSP uses 0-based); **Decision:** Store and display 1-based in evidence and UI; convert to 0-based only at the LSP protocol boundary.
- **code** -- Optional; diagnostic code if provided by server.

items.title: Snapshot file contract
items.statement: MVP evidence is one JSON object per gate run in the lsp-snapshots directory, with capture time, scope, project root, and diagnostic array; MVP captures after iteration and before promotion.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Content:** Single JSON object: `{ "captured_at": "ISO8601", "scope": "changed_files"|"open"|"project", "project_root": "...", "diagnostics": [ {...}, ... ] }`.

- **After run (when gate runs):** Yes. When the LSP gate verifier runs (at tier boundary), it captures the snapshot **at that moment** (after iteration, before promotion). So: **one snapshot per gate run** at the time the gate is evaluated.

items.title: Optional LSP-informed subagent ranking
items.statement: When explicitly enabled, the orchestrator queries diagnostics for a node-related file scope and biases the next subagent ranking toward the language indicated by diagnostic source or file/server mapping; the feature defaults off.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Where in the flow:** When the orchestrator is about to **select a subagent for the next node** (task or subtask), it can optionally query LSP diagnostics for **files in scope** for that node. **Decision:** Default **off**. Config key `orchestrator.lsp_subagent_bias` (bool, default false). When true, call `get_diagnostics_for_paths` and apply bias toward matching-language subagent. If any file has diagnostics (e.g. errors) from a language server X, **prefer** the subagent that matches language X (e.g. rust-analyzer → rust-engineer, pyright → python-pro).

items.title: LSP bias cannot override hard selection authority
items.statement: The canonical bias rules explicitly limit LSP evidence to a ranking hint and preserve the precedence of plan requirements, node overrides, and required_subagents.

evidence.exact_quote: - LSP bias is a **tie-breaker / ranking hint**, not an absolute selector.
- Explicit plan requirements, node override lists, or hard-coded contract needs (for example `required_subagents`) take precedence over LSP bias.

items.title: Timeout, no-server, and empty-scope handling
items.statement: A diagnostic timeout fails with any partial snapshot attached, a file without a language server contributes no diagnostics, and a zero-file scope passes.

evidence.exact_quote: | **Timeout when querying diagnostics** | LspGateVerifier uses a timeout (e.g. `timeout_seconds` from config). On timeout: **fail** the criterion with `actual: "LSP diagnostics query timed out"`. Attach partial snapshot if any diagnostics were collected before timeout. |
| **Empty scope (changed_files/open/project)** | If scope resolves to zero files (e.g. no files changed), gate **passes** (nothing to check). |

items.title: Document ownership boundary
items.statement: LSPSupport remains the owner of the preserved LSP behavior while cross-document ownership is delegated through ContractRefs and boundary notes.

evidence.exact_quote: This source-preserving standardization keeps the owner and consumer boundaries stated in the original document body. During this batch, `Plans/LSPSupport.md` remains the owner doc for the behavior described by its preserved sections, while cross-doc ownership follows the ContractRefs and boundary notes already present in the original text.

items.title: Accepted LSP capability inventory
items.statement: LSPS-004 accepts a broad MVP inventory spanning diagnostics, hover, completion, navigation, code intelligence, timeouts, status, server controls, fallback, and Assistant diagnostics.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP MVP capability inventory includes diagnostics, hover, autocomplete, navigation, inlay hints, semantic highlighting, code actions, code lens, signature help, timeout/cancellation, LSP status UI, per-server disable, fallback behavior, and diagnostics for LLM/Assistant context.

items.title: Unavailable LSP cannot fabricate semantic state
items.statement: The PlanUnit records an explicit negative constraint that unavailable LSP behavior cannot fabricate diagnostics, language responses, or health.

evidence.exact_quote: - Unavailable LSP must not fabricate diagnostics, hover, completion, or healthy semantic capability state.

items.title: Planning units forbid premature executable work
items.statement: The accepted PlanUnits explicitly preserve the planning-only boundary and do not authorize WorkNodes, executable queues, manifests, or production build tasks.

evidence.exact_quote: - No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks are created.

items.title: Blocking-threshold wire tokens conflict
items.statement: The semantic contract names `error` and `error_and_warning`, while the resolved config and field table name `errors` and `errors_and_warnings`. No canonical serialization aliases or migration rule resolves the mismatch.
items.impact: Configuration produced by one normative subsection can be rejected or silently interpreted differently by another, changing whether warnings block promotion.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose canonical tokens and decide whether to accept the singular forms as compatibility aliases.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`error_and_warning`** -- Gate passes if there are **no diagnostics with severity Error or Warning** in scope. Info is ignored.
| `block_on` | string | `"errors"` \| `"errors_and_warnings"` | **`"errors"`** |

items.title: Unavailable-policy enum conflicts
items.statement: The resolved config allows only skip or fail, but the failure table additionally declares pass and server-disconnect behavior depends on it. The persisted schema, UI affordance, and compatibility behavior for pass are not defined.
items.impact: An unavailable or crashed LSP can produce incompatible gate outcomes across implementations.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must decide whether pass is a valid persisted value and distinguish it from skip in gate reporting and promotion semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: | `when_unavailable` | string | `"skip"` \| `"fail"` | **`"skip"`** |

| **LSP client not ready** | Gate does not run, or runs with a **skip** result. **Decision:** When LSP gate is enabled but client not ready: **skip** the criterion; set `actual: "LSP client not ready"`. Config: `lsp_gate.when_unavailable`: `skip` \| `pass` \| `fail`, default **skip**. Gate does not block on LSP startup. |

items.title: Scope resolution is not deterministic
items.statement: Changed-file scope alternates between last iteration and current subtask, and project scope offers non-equivalent bounds such as project-root files or only open documents. No authoritative resolver, precedence, deleted/renamed-file handling, or normalization contract is specified.
items.impact: Identical project state can yield different diagnostic sets and promotion decisions.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must select change provenance, time window, project traversal bound, and path-normalization rules.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`changed_files`** -- Only files that were modified in the last iteration (or in the current subtask). Requires tracking changed paths (e.g. from git diff or execution engine "files touched").
- **`project`** -- All project files that have an LSP server (bounded: e.g. under project root, or only files with open documents). Default: **`changed_files`** to keep checks fast and relevant.

items.title: Diagnostic freshness is unbounded
items.statement: The client may use its existing publishDiagnostics cache and/or trigger a request, but the gate has no document-version, generation, cache-age, synchronization, or stale-response rule before a cached entry can block promotion.
items.impact: A stale error can incorrectly stop work, while stale absence can incorrectly pass a tier.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define freshness, document version matching, cache invalidation, and the wait/quiescence point used at a boundary.

evidence.exact_quote: - Returns: list of diagnostics (path, line, character, severity, message, source) for the given paths. If a path has no server or no diagnostics, it contributes an empty list. The client uses the existing DiagnosticsCache (from `publishDiagnostics`) and/or triggers a request if needed; must respect timeout (e.g. 15 s) and return partial results or error on timeout.

items.title: Timeout interface and partial-result semantics are incomplete
items.statement: Timeout is configured and timeout failure must attach partial evidence, yet the conceptual client signature carries no timeout or cancellation input and its return contract says partial results or error without defining how both diagnostics and timeout state are returned together.
items.impact: The verifier cannot reliably distinguish complete success, timed-out partial success, and a hard error through the shown result type.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must design cancellation, deadline propagation, and a result type that preserves partial diagnostics with a timeout status.

evidence.exact_quote: - Signature (conceptual): `get_diagnostics_for_paths(paths: &[PathBuf], project_root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<LspDiagnosticEntry>, LspGateError>`.

| **Timeout when querying diagnostics** | LspGateVerifier uses a timeout (e.g. `timeout_seconds` from config). On timeout: **fail** the criterion with `actual: "LSP diagnostics query timed out"`. Attach partial snapshot if any diagnostics were collected before timeout. |

items.title: Criterion method identifier is unresolved
items.statement: The integration repeatedly permits either `lsp` or `lsp_gate` as verification_method without selecting a canonical token, alias behavior, or migration rule for stored criteria.
items.impact: Criterion injection and registry lookup can disagree and fail to dispatch the verifier.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must choose one identifier and decide whether the other remains a compatibility alias.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Who calls LSP:** A new verifier **`LspGateVerifier`** (or **`lsp_gate_verifier`**), registered in `VerifierRegistry` (e.g. in `verifier.rs` `register_defaults`). Criterion type: `verification_method: "lsp"` or `"lsp_gate"`.

- **Criterion injection:** When building gate criteria for a tier (e.g. in `build_gate_criteria` or where acceptance criteria are converted to criteria), if `lsp_gate.enabled` is true and the current tier boundary (phase/task/subtask) is in `lsp_gate.tier_boundaries`, add a criterion with `verification_method: "lsp"` (or `"lsp_gate"`) and pass scope/block_on (in criterion params or from shared config). No change to criterion type enum beyond adding this method.

items.title: Global and per-tier config precedence is not resolved
items.statement: The plan permits global configuration or per-tier overrides and recommends a nested override, but does not define merge precedence, partial override behavior, invalid empty boundary handling, or which value the GUI edits.
items.impact: A displayed configuration can resolve differently at phase, task, and subtask boundaries.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define inheritance and merge semantics and expose the effective tier value.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Where:** Verification tab (Settings or Config → Verification). Can be **global** (one setting for all tiers) or **per-tier** (override per phase/task/subtask). Recommendation: global `lsp_gate` with optional per-tier override in tier config.

items.title: Snapshot privacy and lifecycle controls are absent
items.statement: The evidence format persists project_root, file paths, and arbitrary server-provided diagnostic messages, but the window defines no redaction, path containment, file permissions, retention, deletion, encryption, or user-consent rules.
items.impact: Evidence can retain source paths, usernames, workspace topology, and message content beyond the gate run and expose them to later consumers.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must set data minimization, access, retention, and redaction policies and decide whether project_root is stored verbatim.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Content:** Single JSON object: `{ "captured_at": "ISO8601", "scope": "changed_files"|"open"|"project", "project_root": "...", "diagnostics": [ {...}, ... ] }`.
- **message** -- Diagnostic message.

items.title: Evidence storage representation and path form remain optional
items.statement: The first evidence contract permits either a file or embedded snapshot, and diagnostic paths may be relative or absolute. Later file-format text does not explicitly retire embedding or select a canonical path form.
items.impact: GateReport consumers cannot rely on a stable artifact reference or portable path representation.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must select storage/reference semantics and normalize paths for portability and containment.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Where stored:** See §17.2. The snapshot is written to `.puppet-master/evidence/lsp-snapshots/` (or embedded in gate report artifact); the GateReport or EvidenceStore references it (e.g. `evidence_type: "lsp_snapshot"`, path to JSON file).
- **path** -- Relative to project root or absolute; same as LSP URI normalized to path.

items.title: Project-scope collection has no enforceable scale bound
items.statement: Project scope is only illustratively bounded and the top-five rule limits prompt auto-ingestion rather than diagnostic collection, LSP query fan-out, snapshot size, storage quota, or UI rendering.
items.impact: Large repositories can exceed the ten-second default, create unbounded evidence artifacts, or stall user-visible gate reporting.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must establish file/diagnostic/byte limits, batching, truncation markers, quotas, and deterministic ordering.

evidence.exact_quote: - **`project`** -- All project files that have an LSP server (bounded: e.g. under project root, or only files with open documents). Default: **`changed_files`** to keep checks fast and relevant.

Prompt-consumable LSP/debug evidence may auto-ingest at most the top five evidence items by current relevance `/severity`; after that cap, additional diagnostics or trace material enter summarization-only mode unless the user explicitly opens the full runtime artifact.

items.title: Language-to-subagent mapping and multi-language ranking are unspecified
items.statement: Bias derives language from server source or file extension and illustrates two mappings, but does not specify the authoritative mapping owner, conflicting signals, multiple-language aggregation, unavailable matching agents, or stable tie resolution.
items.impact: The same diagnostics can lead to non-repeatable subagent preference outcomes and weak explainability.
items.builder_discretion: A builder must define the mapping registry, aggregation score, fallback candidates, and deterministic tie ordering.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Documentation:** This behavior is specified in **Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md** (Subagent selection from LSP) and summarized here. Implement in the same place that performs `select_for_node`: after building node context, optionally call LSP client `get_diagnostics_for_paths(scope_paths)`; from the returned diagnostics, derive language(s) from `source` or from file extension → server id mapping; then bias subagent selection toward matching language (e.g. add to ProjectContext or NodeContext: "prefer_subagents": ["rust-engineer"] when Rust errors present).

items.title: Selection explainability is advisory
items.statement: The selected bias inputs and outcome are only SHOULD-level persisted, so the contract does not guarantee an audit trail for an LSP-influenced subagent decision.
items.impact: A run can satisfy the selection contract without enough evidence to reproduce or explain the ranking decision.
items.builder_discretion: A builder can omit persistence or choose an arbitrary metadata shape and retention period.

evidence.exact_quote: - The chosen bias inputs and outcome SHOULD be persisted in run metadata or verification evidence so selection remains explainable.

items.title: PlanUnit acceptance oracles do not test runtime behavior
items.statement: The shown PlanUnits validate migration and plan indexing plus source preservation/addressability, but provide no executable acceptance oracle for gate timing, threshold evaluation, snapshot accuracy, failure transitions, UI persistence, or subagent-bias outcomes.
items.impact: Plan conformance can pass while the described product behavior is absent or incorrect.
items.builder_discretion: A later compiler or builder must invent behavioral test fixtures, expected reports, failure injections, and UI/config round-trip assertions.

evidence.exact_quote: acceptance_criteria:
validation_surfaces:
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-migration.py validate --run-dir Plans/.plan_migration/pds-20260611-002-atomize-planunits
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate

items.title: Existing evidence pipeline compatibility is not provable in-window
items.statement: The text requires reuse of an existing VerifierResult, GateReport, and optional EvidenceStore pipeline but does not expose those types or artifact contracts in this window, so compatibility with snapshot references cannot be verified here.
items.impact: Required fields, size limits, serialization, and lifecycle behavior may not accommodate the proposed evidence without changes despite the assertion that no new GateReport field is needed.
items.builder_discretion: Unknown until the owning type contracts are reviewed; this blind window does not authorize that review.

evidence.exact_quote: - **GateReport / evidence:** Use the **existing** evidence pipeline: `VerifierResult` carries `evidence` (e.g. path to snapshot file or artifact id); the gate runner aggregates per-criterion results into `GateReport`; EvidenceStore (if present) persists artifacts per existing rules. No new GateReport field required; LSP snapshot is stored as an artifact referenced by the LSP criterion's result.

items.title: PlanUnit dependency graph omits stated runtime dependencies
items.statement: LSPS-002 declares no dependencies or unblocks even though the authoritative implementation contract requires gate criteria construction, registry dispatch, an LSP client, diagnostics cache, and evidence plumbing.
items.impact: A compiler using PlanUnit metadata can schedule the requirement without the capabilities its own canonical text requires.
items.builder_discretion: A downstream planner must infer dependencies from prose rather than declared PlanUnit edges.

dimension_assessments.summary: Gate timing, pass/fail evaluation, snapshot capture, and optional selection bias are stated, with freshness and exact resolver gaps tracked separately.
The window defines the gate, evidence snapshot, LSP diagnostic query, GUI configuration, and optional subagent ranking capabilities.
Paths, project root, diagnostics, criterion result, and snapshot are identified, but scope resolution and timeout/partial-result representation remain incomplete.
Core contracts exist, but blocking tokens, unavailable enum, method identity, and evidence representation conflict or remain optional.
Boundary evaluation, pass/fail, retry/escalate/stop, skip, timeout failure, no-server, and empty-scope outcomes are substantially explicit.
Verifier, registry, gate runner, and owner docs are assigned authority, but configuration precedence and canonical dispatch identity are unresolved.
LSPSupport ownership and cross-document delegation are explicit; runtime ownership is assigned to named verifier, client, registry, runner, and evidence surfaces.
GateReport, Dashboard, optional toast, EvidenceStore, users, orchestrator selection, and prompt evidence ingestion are named consumers.
The exact Verification-tab controls and failure-reporting surfaces are specified; detailed visual composition is not required for this behavior contract.
Retry, escalation, stop, timeout, missing server, empty scope, and unavailability are covered, but the unavailable enum conflict and partial-timeout API prevent deterministic handling.
Snapshots persist paths, project root, and diagnostic messages without defined minimization, access, redaction, or retention controls.
Criterion results propagate through GateReport to orchestrator and UI, and LSP signals propagate into ranking, but optional explainability and omitted PlanUnit dependency edges weaken traceability.
Capture timing, directory, filename patterns, and timeout default are stated, but evidence lifecycle, quotas, collision handling, and effective config observability are missing.
Changed_files and a ten-second timeout aim to bound cost, but project-scope collection and evidence size have no enforceable limits; top-five prompt ingestion does not bound upstream work.
Conflicting block_on and when_unavailable tokens plus dual verification_method names lack aliases or migration rules.
The document defines observable runtime outcomes, but PlanUnit validation surfaces test plan migration/indexing rather than those outcomes.
Consequential discretion remains in token canonicalization, scope resolution, cache freshness, timeout result shape, storage/path policy, privacy, scale, and subagent ranking.
The review records explicit token conflicts and semantic ambiguities and treats compatibility with unseen existing pipeline types as unknown rather than inventing facts.
